description: This course introduces students to the principles of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) using Java, focusing on core concepts such as classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, and encapsulation. Topics include the Java syntax and semantics, object creation and manipulation, method overloading, access modifiers, interfaces, and abstract classes. The course also covers standard libraries such as java.util and java.io, and explores algorithms for data processing and file handling. Students will implement practical applications using Java, including command-line tools and basic GUI interfaces with Swing. The course emphasizes the use of OOP principles to solve real-world problems through structured programming techniques and design patterns.

clos.text: Define the core principles of Object-Oriented Programming, including encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism, using Java syntax and examples.
Describe the structure and components of Java classes, including constructors, instance variables, and methods, with emphasis on access modifiers and visibility.
Explain the use of inheritance and polymorphism in Java, including method overriding, abstract classes, and interfaces, with practical examples.
Apply Java programming concepts to implement data structures and algorithms for file input/output operations using the java.io package.
Implement basic graphical user interfaces (GUIs) using Java Swing, including event handling and component layout, to demonstrate OOP principles in real-world applications.
